sources_considered.why: Primary research summary documents broader non-tech paid adoption before the post, but does not establish substantial spending prevalence.
Dated primary update establishes the reporting sequence and provides later-period context about adoption and spending.
The accessible summary reports spending intensity across all adopters, without the industry distribution needed to settle this claim.
The live dashboard contains later observations and revisions. Its adoption measures do not settle the substantial-spending claim.

evidence_items.locator: Signal #1: AI adoption is spreading much further than tech

receipt.public_excerpt: Meanwhile, middle-of-the-pack sectors are closing the adoption gap increasingly fast.

evidence_items.explanation: Ramp describes non-tech sectors catching up in paid adoption in its summer reporting. This challenges a broad claim of no diffusion beyond tech, but does not measure how many non-tech firms spend substantial amounts.

evidence_items.locator: Model market share: Anthropic widens its lead, but overall business AI adoption slows

receipt.public_excerpt: new AI adoption continues to grow but is decelerating.

evidence_items.explanation: The August update documents continued adoption growth alongside slowing growth and lower spending among the largest spenders. It concerns the following month and does not provide the required non-tech expenditure distribution.

unresolved_gaps: No representative distribution establishes the share of non-tech businesses making substantial AI expenditures in the target period.
The available adoption trends do not establish whether spending intensity outside tech was broadening.
The claim supplies no spending threshold, and the retrieved evidence does not settle it across ordinary reasonable thresholds.
